suppressions.reason: The Symfony skeleton .gitignore already excludes .env.local files. Replaced by the framework-specific check below, which also covers .env.prod.local.

checks.title: APP_DEBUG is 0 and APP_ENV is prod in production
checks.why: Debug mode serves full stack traces, environment variables and the web profiler to any visitor, which hands an attacker your configuration.
checks.action: Set APP_ENV=prod and APP_DEBUG=0 in the production environment, either in the host's environment variables or in .env.prod.local.

verify.expect: APP_ENV resolves to prod and APP_DEBUG to 0. If nothing prints, confirm both are set in the host's environment instead.

checks.title: No .env.local or .env.prod.local file is tracked in git
checks.why: Those files hold the real database credentials and APP_SECRET. Once committed they stay in history even after deletion, and must be rotated rather than removed.
checks.action: Remove any tracked environment file from the index, confirm it is ignored, then rotate every credential that was ever committed.

verify.expect: Every path reports that it did not match any file. Any path listed back means it is tracked.

checks.title: Dev-only bundles are not enabled in the prod environment
checks.why: The profiler, debug and maker bundles expose routes and internals that should never be reachable in production.
checks.action: Open config/bundles.php and confirm the profiler, debug and maker bundles are scoped to the dev and test environments only.

verify.expect: Each matching line is scoped to dev or test, and none is scoped to all or to prod.

checks.title: Trusted hosts and trusted proxies are configured
checks.why: Without a trusted host list, a forged Host header can poison generated URLs and password reset links. Behind a load balancer, unset trusted proxies means every client appears to come from the balancer.
checks.action: Set framework.trusted_hosts to the domains you serve, and framework.trusted_proxies to the addresses of your load balancer or CDN.

verify.expect: trusted_hosts lists the domains you actually serve, and trusted_proxies is set when the application sits behind a proxy.

checks.title: Production dependencies are installed without dev packages
checks.why: Dev dependencies ship test fixtures, debug tooling and extra code paths to production, enlarging both the attack surface and the deploy artifact.
checks.action: Install with the no-dev and optimize-autoloader flags in the production build step.

verify.expect: The command succeeds and no dev-only package appears in the production install.

checks.title: The production cache is warmed during deploy, not on first request
checks.why: Without a warmed cache the first visitors after each deploy pay the full container and routing compilation cost, and a cold cache under load can stall the whole site.
checks.action: Run the cache clear and cache warmup console commands as part of the deploy, before traffic is switched over.

verify.expect: The prod cache directory exists and contains compiled container files.

checks.title: Production error pages are branded rather than the framework default
checks.why: The default error page tells a visitor which framework you run and reads as a broken site rather than a handled failure.
checks.action: Override the error templates under templates/bundles/TwigBundle/Exception so that 404 and 500 responses match the site's design.

verify.manual: Request a URL that does not exist on the deployed site, then confirm the response is your own styled page and carries a 404 status.

checks.title: Slow work is moved off the request into Messenger
checks.why: Sending mail, generating files or calling third-party APIs inside a request ties response time to systems you do not control, though whether it is worth the queue infrastructure depends on your traffic.
checks.action: Consider dispatching slow operations to a Messenger transport with a worker, rather than running them inline in the controller.
